cluster_summary: This cluster contains vulnerabilities where user-controlled data is embedded into web output (HTML, JavaScript, XML) without proper context-specific escaping, leading to cross-site scripting (XSS) or code injection. The root cause is the assumption that untrusted data is safe for direct inclusion in the output, without applying appropriate encoding for the target context (HTML entity, JavaScript string, XML attribute). The fixes involve using escaping functions or safe DOM APIs to ensure data is treated as text, not executable code.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled or externally supplied XML documents, SOAP messages, XML reports, configuration files, XPath inputs, or XSLT stylesheets into XML parser, XPath, transformer, schema, or SOAP/XML utility code that parses or transforms those documents. Report code paths where DTD declarations, external general entities, external parameter entities, external schema access, or external stylesheet access are not disabled or constrained on the exact parser/transformer instance. Confirm that the guard is enforced before the sensitive effect and remains bound to the same resource, principal, destination, or object that the effect uses. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should disable DOCTYPE and external entity processing, restrict external-access properties, and install a resolver or parser configuration that rejects external resource resolution before parsing.

mechanism.missing_guard: DTD declarations, external general entities, external parameter entities, external schema access, or external stylesheet access are not disabled or constrained on the exact parser/transformer instance
mechanism.name: unsafe XML parser external entity or DTD resolution
mechanism.sink_shape: XML parser, XPath, transformer, schema, or SOAP/XML utility code that parses or transforms those documents
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-controlled or externally supplied XML documents, SOAP messages, XML reports, configuration files, XPath inputs, or XSLT stylesheets
mechanism.typical_fix: disable DOCTYPE and external entity processing, restrict external-access properties, and install a resolver or parser configuration that rejects external resource resolution before parsing

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Use programmatic DOM creation (createElement, setInnerText) instead of string concatenation to automatically encode text content.
sub_patterns.name: Unsafe DOM construction via string concatenation
sub_patterns.root_cause: HTML is built by concatenating untrusted strings directly into a string buffer that is then set as innerHTML, without encoding or safe DOM manipulation.
